content: 1. A study conducted in Jordan in 2012 by Okour included 197 children under the age of 13. Another study in Argentina in 2012 by Pezzani involved 716 children under the age of 17. Additionally, a study in India in 2017 by Ramani examined 114 students. 2. A study by El-Gilany in 2005 found that households with more than three people per room were associated with certain health outcomes. Another study by Hosoglu in 2006 also contributed to this analysis. 3. Skin infections were studied in two cross-sectional studies: one in 161 children under the age of 7 in Australia (Bailie, 2005) and another in 2104 children in Egypt (Hegab, 2015). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 4. Meningococcal disease was investigated in seven studies, including one cohort study in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and the Netherlands (Norheim, 2014), three case-control studies (De Wals, 2005; Deutch, 2004; Olea, 2017), and three cross-sectional studies (Al Jarousha, 2014; Alemayehu, 2017; MacLennan, 2006). These studies involved populations ranging from 74 children in Canada to 35 million people in Scandinavian countries. 5. Rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease were studied in five studies, including two cohort studies (Jaine, 2011; Phillips, 2014) and three case-control studies (Mirabel, 2015; Okello, 2012; Riaz, 2013). These studies included populations such as 1249 cases of acute rheumatic fever in New Zealand and 373,321 deaths from rheumatic heart disease in the UK. 6. Throat, eye, and skin infections were examined in a cross-sectional study involving 1896 households in India (Firdaus, 2013). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 7. Risk factors for water, sanitation, and hygiene were studied in a cross-sectional study involving 701 people in Guatemala (Rao, 2010). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 8. Epstein-Barr virus was studied in a cohort of 12,457 children under the age of 14 in the UK (Gares, 2017). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 9. Helicobacter pylori infection was examined in a cross-sectional study involving 7398 people over the age of 3 in the USA (Krueger, 2015). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 10. Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was studied in two studies: one ecological study in the UK with nearly 900,000 residents (Auguet, 2016) and one case-control study in Brazil involving 117 HIV-infected youth under the age of 25 (Vieira, 2016). 11. Toxoplasma gondii infection was studied in a case-control study involving 375 miners in Mexico (Alvarado-Esquivel, 2016). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 12. Mental health outcomes, including stress and sleep disorders, were studied in various populations. For example, a cross-sectional study in Greenland involved 839 people (Riva, 2014b), and another study in the USA examined 371 low-income adults (Chambers, 2016). The quality of evidence was generally low to very low. 13. Drug and alcohol abuse was studied in a cross-sectional study involving 2678 youths in Iraq (Al-Hemiary, 2015). The quality of evidence was rated as high. 14. Anxiety and depression were studied in three studies, including a cohort study in the UK involving 6341 people (Barnes, 2011) and a cross-sectional study in Greenland involving 3066 people (Riva, 2014a). The quality of evidence was low. 15. Schizophrenia was studied in a cohort study involving 11,015 people in Israel, including 104 cases (Kimhy, 2006). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 16. Psychological distress was studied in two cross-sectional studies: one in 4326 households in India (Firdaus, 2017) and another in New Zealand with over 13,800 responses (Pierse, 2016). The quality of evidence was very low. 17. Suicide ideation and self-esteem were studied in a cross-sectional study involving 452 Inuit participants aged 15–30 in Canada (Gray, 2016). The quality of evidence was rated as very low. 18. Autonomic nervous system reactivity and externalizing behavior problems were studied in a cohort of children under the age of 7 from 99 families in the USA (Waters, 2017). The quality of evidence was very low. 19. Emotional symptoms and inattention-hyperactivity were studied in a cross-sectional study involving 1233 children aged 2–5 in Canada (Kohen, 2015). The quality of evidence was very low.
